Tim Cook's tenure as Apple CEO is entering its final weeks, with John Ternus set to take over the top role on September 1. Bank of America analyst Wamsi Mohan believes Ternus could usher in a bolder, more risk-taking new era for Apple.

Ternus is expected to take greater risks with new products, acquisitions, and R&D once he becomes CEO.

The Apple CEO transition is nearly complete. So far, the company has heavily emphasised the continuity Ternus will bring to the role.

However, not everyone on Wall Street is convinced Ternus will follow Cook's playbook so closely.

In a research note obtained by The Street, Bank of America analyst Wamsi Mohan reiterated his strong "buy" rating on Apple, with one key element being the expectation that Ternus will carry on Cook's legacy while also having a stronger "willingness to take risks." Here's what Moz Farukh had to say:

The firm highlighted that Apple's abandoning of its "net cash neutral" goal is seen as an early signal that management is more willing to deploy capital. This would translate into higher R&D spending, more capex, and larger-scale acquisitions — all areas that were not a focus during Cook's era. Bank of America believes that under Ternus, Apple could more quickly move into several entirely new product categories, including AI glasses, AirPods with cameras, smart rings, smart home, personal assistants, and robotics.

Ultimately, Bank of America believes Ternus will carry on Cook's legacy of building Apple into a highly profitable global business, but also expects him to leverage the company's current strong position to make bolder moves going forward.

We don't expect to see any major changes as soon as Ternus takes over as CEO, but in the coming months, any potential differences in priorities could gradually emerge.

What are your expectations for John Ternus as Apple's CEO? Let us know in the comments.
